==History==
DetonatioN FocusMe is one of the first competitive League of Legends teams in Japan, forming in 2013. <ref name="detonation history1">{{cite web|url=https://www.redbull.com/us-en/detonation-gaming-japanese-esports|title=DetonatioN Gaming: Japan's Vanguard|author=Cameron Gilbert|publisher=RedBull|date=2017-02-20|language={{Flag|usuk}} English}}</ref> The roster of [[gorira13]], [[Anelace]], [[Ceros]], [[iimitai]] and [[PresidentMaa]] made their international debut at the [[Intel_Extreme_Masters/Season_VIII/Singapore|IEM Singapore Amateur Tournament]] at the end of 2013, where they were eliminated by Hong Kong team [[CGA LEGENDs]] in a 2-1 loss. From here on, DetonatioN FocusMe won the [[LJL/2014/Summer|2014 LJL Summer Split]], and beat [[Rascal Jester]] in the [[LJL/Grand_Finals/2014|2014 LJL Grand Finals]].

In 2015, the LoL esports circuit was expanded, with Japan now participating in the International Wildcard Tournament. With a win in the [[LJL/2015/Season_1|First season of 2015]], DFM qualified for [[International_Wildcard_Invitational/2015|IWCI 2015]]. The roster consisting of [[BonziN]], [[Astarore]], [[Ceros]], [[Yutapongo]] and [[KazuXD]] placed 6th, only beating 7th place finishers [[Kaos Latin Gamers]]. The roster stuck together despite this, and even with a 2nd place in the [[LJL/2015/Season_1|second LJL season]], they qualified for the [[LJL/Grand_Finals/2015|2015 Grand Finals]], where they beat [[Ozone Rampage]] 3-2 to qualify for the [[International_Wildcard_Tournament/2015/Turkey|International Wildcard Tournament]]. DetonatioN FocusMe placed 4th and last with a ''2-4'' record.

DetonatioN FocusMe once again won the spring split in 2016, going undefeated (13-0). Despite regional dominance, they were unable to put up a great performance at [[International_Wildcard/2016/Invitational|IWCI 2016]], ending with a 3/-/4 record and a 5th place exit. With a second place in the [[LJL/2016/Summer|Summer split]], DetonatioN FocusMe did not qualify for the second international event. This would continue in 2017, where the team placed 2nd in both [[LJL/2017/Spring|Spring]] and [[LJL/2017/Summer|Summer]], failing to qualify for any international event.

In 2018, DFM once again went undefeated in the regular season, but [[PENTAGRAM]] beat them 3-0 in the finals to take away their slot at [[Mid_Season_Invitational/2018|MSI 2018]]. They managed to win the [[LJL/2018/Summer|Summer Season]] with a 3-1 finals victory against [[Unsold Stuff Gaming]], securing a slot in the [[World_Championship/2018|Worlds 2018 Play-ins]], where they were eliminated by [[EDward Gaming]] in the second play-in stage. 2019 consisted of more regional dominance, winning both splits, but DetonatioN FocusMe did not impress internationally, not making it out of their [[Mid-Season_Invitational/2019|MSI 2019]] and [[World_Championship/2019|Worlds 2019]] play-in groups.

Continuing their regional dominance, DetonatioN FocusMe won the [[LJL/2020/Spring|2020 LJL Spring Split]], but with [[Mid-Season_Invitational/2020|MSI 2020]] being cancelled, the team was not able to show what they're capable of internationally. In [[LJL/2020/Summer|Summer]], DetonatioN FocusMe was beat by [[V3 Esports]] in a close 5-game grand final. Ahead of 2021, it was announced that [[Aria]] joined the team, replacing long-time member [[Ceros]]. [[Kazu]] also returned to the starting roster after coaching the team, due to import regulations. The team won the [[LJL/2021/Spring|2021 LJL Spring Season]], but was eliminated in their [[Mid-Season_Invitational/2021|MSI 2021]] group with [[DAMWON Gaming]] and [[Cloud9]] placing ahead of them in group C. In the [[LJL/2021/Summer|2021 LJL Summer Season]], [[Gaeng]] returned to the starting roster, and DFM qualified for [[World_Championship/2021|Worlds 2021]] by securing yet another LJL title. At Worlds, DetonatioN FocusMe became the first Japanese team ever to qualify for the group stage<ref name="detonation first jp team qualify ">{{cite web|url=https://www.esports.com/en/dfm-becomes-the-first-ljl-team-in-history-to-qualify-for-the-worlds-group-stage-282197|title=DFM becomes the first LJL team in history to qualify for the Worlds Group Stage|author=Blaine Polhamus|publisher=esports.com|date=2021-10-08|language={{Flag|usuk}} English}}</ref>, where they ended with a 0-6 record, losing all their games against [[T1]], [[EDward Gaming]], and [[100 Thieves]].

DFM needed two changes in their roster for the 2022 season when Mid laner [[Aria]] left the team for [[KT Rolster]] and was replaced by [[Yaharong]] and Support [[Gaeng]] announced his retirement as a player to go to the Korean Military service. Even with those roster changes, DFM was able to win both [[LJL/2022/Spring|Spring]] and [[LJL/2022/Summer|Summer]] of 2022 and qualified for [[World Championship/2022|Worlds]], where they were eliminated only in the second round of Play-In, leaving the tournament with wins against [[Evil Geniuses]] and [[Royal Never Give Up]].

Before the 2023 year, [[Evi]] announced his departure to the [[LEC]] after five years of playing for DFM and [[tol2]] arrived from the Academy team to replace him. With many problems his backstage evolving harassment from the team’s Staff to tol2, Coaches [[Kazu]] and [[Ceros]] had their contracts terminated. Following that incident, DetonatioN FocusMe and tol2 also agreed to terminate his contract. <ref name="dfm incident">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YXsIFhL3P9g&t=1617s7|title=tol2 and DFM. - An extensive summary of an LJL drama|author=The Jesport Hub|publisher=Youtube|date=2023-07-08|language={{Flag|usuk}} English}}</ref> DFM won [[LJL/2023/Spring|Spring]] and [[LJL/2023/Summer|Summer]] of 2023 and for the first time in their history, they left both [[Mid-Season_Invitational|MSI]] and [[World Championship|World Championship]] without a single victory.
